title: Algorithm's Auction
summary: Every move is a strategy. Every bid is a gamble.
description: Ready for a challenge that's more than just coding? Whether you're a beginner or a problem-solving enthusiast, Algorithm's Auction is specially curated for ECS students across all years. Get ready for 2 days of logic, strategy, competitive bidding and exciting challenges.

syllabus.desc: Binary search variations, rotated arrays, custom comparator sort logic, and two-pointer search patterns.
Activity selection, interval merging, coin change optimal selection, and greedy decision trees.
Recursive breakdown, merge sort paradigms, binary exponentiation, and peak element discovery.
Adjacency representations, BFS queue traversal, DFS recursion, and connected component counting.

bidding_rules.title: Virtual Coin Purse
bidding_rules.description: Every registered team receives a fixed purse of virtual auction coins at the beginning of Day 2. Coins are used to bid on problem statements of varying point weights.

bidding_rules.title: Open & Blind Bidding Tiers
bidding_rules.description: Problems are categorized into Bronze (100 pts), Silver (250 pts), and Gold (500 pts). Teams place bids to lock down problems. The highest bidder secures the problem.

bidding_rules.title: The Steal Deal Window
bidding_rules.description: If a team fails to pass test cases on their acquired problem within the designated timer, the problem is unlocked for live steal bids at a discounted coin price.

bidding_rules.title: Net Scoring Formula
bidding_rules.description: Final ranking = (Points from passed test cases) - (Total coins spent on auctions). Conservative bidding paired with accurate coding yields the championship score.

faqs.question: Do I need prior competitive coding experience?
faqs.answer: Not at all! Day 1 is specifically designed as "Learn the Logic", where senior mentors walk through algorithm patterns with interactive mini-challenges so everyone is prepared for the Day 2 auction.

faqs.question: Can First-Year (FE) ECS students take part?
faqs.answer: Yes, absolutely! Algorithm's Auction is open to FE, SE, TE, and BE students of the Department of Electronics & Computer Science. Beginner-friendly problems and mentor support are provided.

faqs.question: What is the team size and composition?
faqs.answer: You can register individually (solo) or as a team of up to 3 students. Solo participants can also be paired with peers during the Day 1 team formation mixer.

faqs.question: What do I need to bring?
faqs.answer: Bring your laptop with an IDE or compiler installed for your preferred language (C++, Python, Java, or C), a charger, and your college ID card.

faqs.question: Will all participants receive certificates?
faqs.answer: Yes. All registered attendees who complete both days will receive an official Certificate of Participation from the Department of Electronics & Computer Science × FLUX-ECS.

title: IoTA Archives
description: IoTA Archives was an exhibition organised by the ECS department at VESIT as part of the induction programme for newly admitted FE students. It gave the new batch a chance to see live robotic demonstrations, embedded projects, and interact directly with their seniors.

labs.label: Embedded Systems Lab
labs.description: The Embedded Systems & Edge Computing Lab was the active robotics wing. Senior students set up live demonstrations of remote-controlled cars, obstacle-avoiding robotic chassis with ultrasonic sensors, and custom sensor rigs. First-year students gathered around the workbenches and floor runs, asking questions and experiencing their first hands-on look at embedded systems.
projects: Obstacle-avoiding robot with HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor and L298N motor driver
Remote-controlled car with custom RF transmitter-receiver pair
FPGA demo board running an LED pattern synthesised in VHDL
Custom sensor rig reading temperature, humidity, and light levels over I²C

labs.label: Basic Electrical Lab
labs.description: Lab 203 hosted hands-on demonstrations and technical discussions around the electrical test benches and computer monitors. Seniors walked freshmen through circuitry, project architectures, computer vision classifiers, and logic design.
projects: Bench test equipment walkthrough & circuit debugging
Real-time object detection using a pre-trained YOLO model
A full-stack student attendance portal built with React and Node.js
A sorting algorithm visualiser showing bubble, merge, and quicksort in real time

labs.label: Tinkerers' Lab
labs.description: In the Tinkerers' Lab, seniors showcased assembled obstacle-avoiding chassis and sat down with freshers to discuss competitive programming, open-source contributions, hardware prototyping, and what to expect from the ECS curriculum.
projects: Live demonstration of obstacle-avoiding robot chassis
Interactive Q&A on competitive programming and hackathons
Open-source contribution demo — Git workflows and submitting pull requests
FLUX-ECS student cohort guidance and roadmap
